newsitem.title: TURKEY: Third minister quits Turkey's Islamist-led govt.
newsitem.headline: Third minister quits Turkey's Islamist-led govt.

text.p: A conservative minister quit Turkey's Islamist-led coalition on Saturday, private NTV reported, further weakening the government's grip on power.

Isilay Saygin, a state minister responsible for family and women's affairs, had been a steady critic of the government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader. Her resignation was widely expected.
NTV said Saygin announced her departure at a news conference in the western port city of Izmir. It gave no other details.

Two other ministers from the junior partner conservatives of the True Path Party resigned in April in protest at Erbakan's refusal to heed military-backed demands for a crackdown on Islamist activism.
The two have since held a series of consultations with members of the pro-Western True Path, as well as opposition figures, to craft an "Islamist-free government".
Opposition parties on Friday submitted a censure motion against the government. The coalition is clinging to a slim majority and its prospects remain uncertain.
